title: The Sheltered Shore
premise: An original restoration-planning fiction for a sheltered estuary. Local surveys determine what belongs here; a living shoreline is not a universal answer to coastal hazards.

items.label: Coir roll
items.description: A bounded coir roll prepared for this sheltered-bank project.

items.label: Marsh plugs
items.description: Native marsh seedlings grown in nursery trays. Several weeks of nursery care pass in this fictional step.

items.label: Planted coir module
items.description: A small planted coir module that can be carried to the bank. It is not a portable shoreline.

items.label: Season report
items.description: A record for continued assessment, not a certificate that the shoreline is restored.

items.label: Seasonal photos
items.description: Photographs from a later season document what happened; the act of making a report does not establish that the intervention succeeded.

recipes.description: Nursery time passes as the native seedlings establish. Biological growth is compressed, not instantaneous.
Nursery-grown marsh plugs are established in a bounded coir module. Placement installs that same module at the sheltered bank.

stages.title: Survey the estuary
stages.speaker: The coastal ecologist
stages.motivation: This bank is sheltered, but it is retreating. Make a shoreline plan from the tide and site records.

area.label: Survey the estuary
area.travelText: We are taking the useful things with us. Earlier creations remain where we made them.

stages.title: Plant the sheltered bank
stages.speaker: The nursery keeper
stages.motivation: Our survey supports native marsh plants here. Set the planted coir module at the Sheltered bank.

area.label: Plant the sheltered bank
area.travelText: We are taking the useful things with us. Earlier creations remain where we made them.

caches.label: The restoration nursery
caches.narrative: The nursery carries locally appropriate plants, coir, stakes, shell and reef materials—not every coast needs all of them.

objectives.text: Place the planted coir module at the Sheltered bank.

stages.title: A season of watching
stages.speaker: The coastal ecologist
stages.motivation: Installing a project is not the same as proving it works. Make a season report from the monitoring record.

area.label: A season of watching
area.travelText: We are taking the useful things with us. Earlier creations remain where we made them.

caches.label: The field team returns
caches.narrative: Survey poles and photographs from a later season arrive with the field team. Time has passed in the story.

sources.title: NOAA: What is a living shoreline?

notes: NOAA supports the general restoration approach, not this fictional engineering design.
Reef module is optional discovery, not forced into every site. No claim that plants prevent every storm or that survey photos alone prove causal success.
